I will keep all 2.2 mu in chili this year because my land is small, I know this crop well after many years, and with some family labor off-farm I need something I already understand and can manage steadily. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on a hybrid chili seed to reduce risk and improve stand and yield. I will prepare the field with rotary tillage because it is easier for me on a small plot and gives a fine seedbed for transplanting. I will use moderate fertilizer: enough nitrogen to support growth, phosphorus for root establishment, and potassium for fruit setting and quality, but not too much because my area is small and I want to control cost. I will irrigate several times through establishment, flowering, and fruiting, since chili responds well to steady moisture but I do not want waterlogging. I will spray pesticides a few times when needed to control the usual insects and diseases and protect yield. With my experience, irrigation access, and careful input use, I expect a solid yield rather than pushing for the highest possible one.
